summary: OWASP Phase 3 — IDOR closure on periodization V2 (/api/v2/*) fully validated against the preview backend. 28/28 pytest passing in /app/backend/tests/test_owasp_phase3_v2_idor.py. (1) Owner regression (Coach A test@train.com): GET/PUT /api/v2/macrociclos/{id}, GET/PUT /api/v2/mesociclos/{id}, GET /api/v2/microciclos/{id}, GET/PUT /api/v2/sesiones/{id}, GET /api/v2/planes/{id}/completo, /metricas, /historico all return 200 against a freshly built plan -> macro -> meso -> micro -> sesion -> ejercicio chain. (2) IDOR blocked: a brand-new Coach B token attacking Coach A's IDs returns 404 on every endpoint — macros (GET+PUT), mesos (GET+PUT), micros (GET), sesiones (GET+PUT), POST /api/v2/macrociclos/{A_macro}/mesociclos, POST /api/v2/sesiones/{A_sesion}/ejercicios, GET /api/v2/planes/{A_plan}/completo, /historico, /metricas. The get_plan_completo fallback chain does NOT leak Coach A's plan to Coach B because Coach B owns no V2 plans. (3) Previous regression intact: login returns token+refresh_token; /api/training-plans, /api/athletes, /api/plan-templates/levels return 200; security headers (X-Frame-Options=DENY, X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff, Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security) present; iter_87 IDOR on /api/sessions/{id}/complete still returns 404 for Coach B.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/periodization_v2.py::_own_plan/_own_macro/_own_meso/_own_micro/_own_sesion uniformly return 404 'no encontrado' both when the entity is missing and when caller is not the owner — correct, no info-leak (matches sessions.py pattern from iter_87).

routes/periodization_v2.py::get_plan_completo has 4 fallback strategies (exact match, _v1_id mapping, training_plans name match, best populated V2 plan). Each fallback is scoped to {coach_id: user['id']} so cross-coach leakage is structurally impossible. Verified: Coach B with no V2 plans cannot resolve Coach A's plan_id — returns 404 as expected.

routes/periodization_v2.py::update_ejercicio and DELETE /ejercicios-sesion/{ej_id} correctly look up the ejercicio first, then call _own_sesion(db, ej['sesion_id'], uid). Same pattern for capacidades via _own_plan. Good defense-in-depth.

POTENTIAL ISSUE (NOT BLOCKING): There is no public POST /api/v2/macrociclos endpoint — macros are only created via /api/v2/seed, /api/v2/sync-from-v1/{v1_plan_id}, or direct DB insert. If the V2 UI expects to create macrociclos directly, this gap may surface later. Not in scope for Phase 3 IDOR.

routes/periodization_v2.py::get_plan_alertas (/api/v2/planes/{id}/alertas) is NOT guarded by _own_plan — it calls validar_cambio_completo(db, plan_id) directly without checking coach_id. Any logged-in coach can query any plan's alertas. Suggest adding `await _own_plan(db, plan_id, user['id'])` at the top. Out of scope of this run but worth a follow-up.

Pydantic schemas MesocicloCreate/SesionCreate/EjercicioSesionCreate still require macrociclo_id/microciclo_id/sesion_id in the body even though the parent id is in the URL path — leads to confusing 422 if the client only sends the URL id. Suggest making these Optional and overriding from the path param. Cosmetic.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite at /app/backend/tests/test_owasp_phase3_v2_idor.py is fully repeatable — each run creates a unique plan name and Coach B email. Uses pymongo directly for setup (MONGO_URL=mongodb://localhost:27017, DB_NAME=train_db). If running back-to-back, slowapi 10/min on /auth/login may cause flakiness; wait ~60s between runs. The mongo.login_attempts.delete_many({email: test@train.com}) call at session-start protects Coach A from accidental lockouts. iter_87 test_owasp_phase2.py + iter_86 test_security_hardening.py remain valid alongside this Phase 3 suite. NOTE for the next agent: /api/v2/planes/{id}/alertas currently has no ownership check — if hardening that endpoint, add a regression test here.
